jobs.description:
Description:

**Location**: Los Angeles, CA (50% travel)

**Position**: Full-Time

**Reports To**: Director of Customer Experience

TGR Solutions, Inc. designs and builds autonomous robots for regulated environments and is based in the heart of Los Angeles, California. TGR develops robotics solutions from the ground up and builds integrated systems that help organizations apply robotics and AI to demanding work.

TGR’s flagship product line, the A1 ADIBOT, is a fully autonomous UV-C disinfection robot that is deployed in facilities around the world. TGR team members come from diverse disciplines and backgrounds and share a hands-on approach to building robotics products.

**Job Description:**

The Implementation Specialist, Life Sciences brings ADIBOT autonomous UV-C disinfection robots into GMP environments and makes them part of how each site runs. A new robot in a classified area changes a validated state, so the job is as much about change control, qualification, and documentation as it is about operator training.

You will own each life sciences account on site from purchase order through its first 90 days. You will work with the customer's QA, Validation, Microbiology, Facilities, EHS, and Operations teams, and with TGR Customer Success, Technical Support, and Sales.

**Responsibilities:**

* Plan each deployment around the customer's contamination control strategy and change control process, so the robot enters the site as a documented, risk-assessed addition to its cleaning and disinfection program.
* Assess site readiness before delivery, including classified areas, airlocks, material transfer routes, doorways, charging, network access, and the rules for running cycles.
* Supply the technical package for the customer's change control: equipment description, UV-C safety data, and inputs to the risk assessment.
* Support the customer's QA team on site through IQ/OQ/PQ while they execute and approve the protocols.
* Become the subject matter expert on the robot and its disinfection protocols. Advise QA and Microbiology on available measurement options, such as dosimetry and cycle records, within TGR-approved claims, and supply robot cycle records for the validation package.
* Answer QA questions on how cycle records are generated, stored, and exported.
* Train and certify operators in UV-C safety, and help the customer write SOPs, work instructions, and training records.
* Review fleet data with each customer, resolve operational bottlenecks, and identify areas for expansion.
* Notify customers of firmware updates and support their change assessment before and after each update.
* Hand each account to Customer Success at day 90 with open items, training records, and a utilization baseline.
* Bring field learnings back to Product and Engineering.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, microbiology or biotechnology, or equivalent work experience.
* 2 to 4 years of field-based, customer-facing technical work, ideally in pharma, biotech, or medical device manufacturing.
* Working knowledge of gowning and work inside classified areas, plus ISO 14644, EU GMP Annex 1, and good documentation practice under GMP regulations.
* Experience with IQ/OQ/PQ and change control, whether you wrote, executed, or supported the protocols.
* Hands-on experience deploying or servicing complex machinery, and confidence troubleshooting hardware and software on site. Network troubleshooting experience is a plus.
* Familiarity with environmental monitoring and cleaning validation.
* Clear technical writing for SOPs, work instructions, and training records.
* Ability to travel 60%, including some weekends.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, military/veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. We actively encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply and believe that a diverse workforce contributes to the strength and success of our organization. jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Cell Biology & Assay Development
jobs.description:
### **About DeepOrigin**

Deep Origin is building ambitious science in a fast-moving environment, combining AI and physics-based methods with wet-lab biology to advance drug discovery. The people who thrive here are accountable, adaptable, rigorous, humble, and direct. Across roles, we look for:

* **Ownership through to the result.** An experiment isn't done until the data are analyzed, the conclusion is written down, and whoever needs it next has it.
* **Judgment under incomplete information.** You resolve what you need to know, commit to a defensible course of action, and revise when the evidence warrants it.
* **Exacting about the work, unguarded about yourself.** You hold data to a standard that survives scrutiny, and you drop your own interpretation when someone shows you better evidence.
* **Transparency as a working habit.** You surface problems while they are cheap to fix, and you explain your results so chemists, engineers, and computational colleagues can act on them.

### **About the role**

We are hiring a hands-on **Senior Research Associate** to build and run the cell-based assays and engineered cell lines behind our drug discovery programs. You will work day to day with a senior scientist in R&D, owning bench execution while helping shape assay strategy.

Your core work: maintaining mammalian cell lines, engineering them with RNP-based CRISPR (knockouts and knock-ins), generating validated stable lines, and turning them into robust functional assays. The data you generate feeds directly into AI and physics-based compound design, so quality and reproducibility matter as much as throughput.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

 **Requirements**  

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in biology, cell biology, bioengineering, biochemistry, immunology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Relevant hands-on laboratory experience
* Demonstrated mammalian cell culture experience with strong aseptic technique, including routine maintenance of multiple lines in parallel.
* Hands-on experience with CRISPR gene editing: knockout generation, and ideally knock-in, with validation of edited clones.
* Experience with transient transfection, and with generating and validating stable cell lines, including clonal selection and banking.
* Experience executing at least one cell-based assay readout, such as flow cytometry, plate-based viability, reporter, or proliferation assays.
* Ability to analyze data, assess assay quality, communicate findings clearly, and work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary setting.
* Commitment to laboratory safety, research integrity, accurate documentation, and responsible handling of biological materials.

### **Nice to have qualifications**

* Hands-on RNP-based CRISPR knockout and knock-in using Lonza Nucleofector platforms (4D-Nucleofector or equivalent), including program and buffer selection for the target cell type.
* Experience with high-throughput or automated assay platforms, including 96- or 384-channel electronic pipetting systems and benchtop pipetting robots (INTEGRA VIAFLO, MINI 96, VOYAGER, ASSIST PLUS or comparable), and multimode plate readers.
* Experience developing or optimizing BRET, TR-FRET/HTRF, or related proximity-based assay formats .
* Molecular biology bench skills: construct and primer design, cloning, qPCR or digital PCR, Western blot.
* Drug discovery experience in biotech or pharma, including work on a target-to-lead or lead-optimization program.
* Familiarity with assay qualification concepts: design of experiments, dose-response analysis, curve fitting, acceptance criteria, and statistical assessment of assay variability.
* Experience with neuronal or other CNS-relevant cell models. .
* Experience with multiplexed editing, including triple knockouts or combined knockout and knock-in lines.

### **Key responsibilities**

**Mammalian cell culture**

* Culture, expand, and maintain mammalian cell lines under strict aseptic technique; monitor health, viability, density, and passage history.
* Maintain cryopreserved stocks, run mycoplasma and identity checks, and keep accurate lineage records.

**Genome engineering**

* Optimize RNP-based CRISPR/Cas editing in mammalian cell lines: single and double knockouts.
* Design and execute targeted knock-in strategies, including donor design, delivery optimization, and editing-efficiency assessment.
* Genotype and validate edits by sequencing, qPCR or digital PCR, and protein-level readouts.

**Stable cell line generation**

* Perform transient transfections to test constructs quickly, optimizing reagent, nucleic acid amount, and harvest timing, and confirming expression before committing to a stable line.
* Generate stable lines using viral and non-viral delivery; perform clonal selection, expansion, functional validation, and banking.
* Characterize clones for expression level, assay performance, and stability over passage.

**Cell-based assay development**

* Develop, optimize, and run functional assays: plate-based, reporter and proximity-based assays; flow cytometry; and other cellular functional readouts.
* Optimize seeding density, stimulation conditions, dose range, incubation time, controls, and acceptance criteria to improve sensitivity, dynamic range, and reproducibility.
* Prepare test articles, reagents, controls, and assay plates according to established protocols and study plans .

**Data, documentation, and communication**

* Analyze dose-response data, fit curves, assess assay quality (Z', signal window, variability), and flag trends, outliers, and deviations.
* Keep complete, timely records in the electronic lab notebook, consistent with data-integrity expectations.
* Present results at team meetings and contribute figures and data to technical reports.

**Lab operations**

* Troubleshoot routine assay and culture

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

  

**About the role**

The QC Technician is the last check between our electronics and the field. You will flash firmware onto circuit boards every day, run functional tests, and make sure every board that leaves the bench is correctly programmed, traceable, and working.

This is a hands-on, bench-based role on the hardware production team. You will work closely with hardware and firmware engineers, follow documented procedures, and flag anything that looks off before it reaches a vehicle.

  

**What you'll do**

* Flash bootloaders, firmware, and configuration files onto PCBs and modules using programming fixtures, JTAG/SWD debuggers, USB/serial tools, and in-house scripts.
* Confirm the correct firmware version and configuration is loaded on every board, matched to the build order, and run batch flashing efficiently while keeping error rates near zero.
* Run functional and power-on tests after flashing, following test procedures and checklists; visually inspect boards for physical defects such as damaged components, solder issues, bent pins, and connector damage.
* Use multimeters, power supplies, and basic test equipment to check voltages and continuity.
* Separate passing and failing units, and tag failures clearly for engineering review. Write clear failure reports with symptoms, steps taken, and photos where useful.
* Log serial numbers, firmware versions, test results, and failures in our tracking system or spreadsheets, label boards and keep inventory of programmed, tested, and failed units accurate.
* Do first-level troubleshooting on failed flashes and tests: re-seat connections, check cables, retry, and swap fixtures–escalate recurring or unexplained failures to hardware and firmware engineers with enough detail to act on.
* Follow ESD-safe handling and keep the bench, fixtures, and tools clean, calibrated, and organized, suggest improvements to procedures, fixtures, and scripts that cut cycle time or errors.
* Help keep work instructions and checklists up to date as firmware and hardware change, and support new product introductions and engineering builds when needed.

  

**What we're looking for**

* High school diploma or equivalent; technical certificate or associate degree in electronics or a related field is a plus.
* 3+ year of hands-on experience in electronics manufacturing, test, QC, or a similar bench role.
* Comfortable handling PCBs and small components with ESD-safe practices.
* Basic use of a multimeter and bench power supply.
* Comfortable on a linux computer: running programs or scripts from instructions, using a command line at an intermediate level, and entering data accurately in spreadsheets or tracking tools.
* Able to follow written procedures exactly and recognize when something doesn't match them, clear written and verbal communication for logging results and reporting failures.
* Reliable, consistent, and comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work.
* Background in automotive, robotics, or heavy equipment electronics preferred.
* IPC-A-610 or IPC J-STD-001 certification, or working knowledge of PCB workmanship standards preferred.

new_jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Cell Biology & Assay Development
new_jobs.description:
### **About DeepOrigin**

Deep Origin is building ambitious science in a fast-moving environment, combining AI and physics-based methods with wet-lab biology to advance drug discovery. The people who thrive here are accountable, adaptable, rigorous, humble, and direct. Across roles, we look for:

* **Ownership through to the result.** An experiment isn't done until the data are analyzed, the conclusion is written down, and whoever needs it next has it.
* **Judgment under incomplete information.** You resolve what you need to know, commit to a defensible course of action, and revise when the evidence warrants it.
* **Exacting about the work, unguarded about yourself.** You hold data to a standard that survives scrutiny, and you drop your own interpretation when someone shows you better evidence.
* **Transparency as a working habit.** You surface problems while they are cheap to fix, and you explain your results so chemists, engineers, and computational colleagues can act on them.

### **About the role**

We are hiring a hands-on **Senior Research Associate** to build and run the cell-based assays and engineered cell lines behind our drug discovery programs. You will work day to day with a senior scientist in R&D, owning bench execution while helping shape assay strategy.

Your core work: maintaining mammalian cell lines, engineering them with RNP-based CRISPR (knockouts and knock-ins), generating validated stable lines, and turning them into robust functional assays. The data you generate feeds directly into AI and physics-based compound design, so quality and reproducibility matter as much as throughput.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

 **Requirements**  

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in biology, cell biology, bioengineering, biochemistry, immunology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Relevant hands-on laboratory experience
* Demonstrated mammalian cell culture experience with strong aseptic technique, including routine maintenance of multiple lines in parallel.
* Hands-on experience with CRISPR gene editing: knockout generation, and ideally knock-in, with validation of edited clones.
* Experience with transient transfection, and with generating and validating stable cell lines, including clonal selection and banking.
* Experience executing at least one cell-based assay readout, such as flow cytometry, plate-based viability, reporter, or proliferation assays.
* Ability to analyze data, assess assay quality, communicate findings clearly, and work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary setting.
* Commitment to laboratory safety, research integrity, accurate documentation, and responsible handling of biological materials.

### **Nice to have qualifications**

* Hands-on RNP-based CRISPR knockout and knock-in using Lonza Nucleofector platforms (4D-Nucleofector or equivalent), including program and buffer selection for the target cell type.
* Experience with high-throughput or automated assay platforms, including 96- or 384-channel electronic pipetting systems and benchtop pipetting robots (INTEGRA VIAFLO, MINI 96, VOYAGER, ASSIST PLUS or comparable), and multimode plate readers.
* Experience developing or optimizing BRET, TR-FRET/HTRF, or related proximity-based assay formats .
* Molecular biology bench skills: construct and primer design, cloning, qPCR or digital PCR, Western blot.
* Drug discovery experience in biotech or pharma, including work on a target-to-lead or lead-optimization program.
* Familiarity with assay qualification concepts: design of experiments, dose-response analysis, curve fitting, acceptance criteria, and statistical assessment of assay variability.
* Experience with neuronal or other CNS-relevant cell models. .
* Experience with multiplexed editing, including triple knockouts or combined knockout and knock-in lines.

### **Key responsibilities**

**Mammalian cell culture**

* Culture, expand, and maintain mammalian cell lines under strict aseptic technique; monitor health, viability, density, and passage history.
* Maintain cryopreserved stocks, run mycoplasma and identity checks, and keep accurate lineage records.

**Genome engineering**

* Optimize RNP-based CRISPR/Cas editing in mammalian cell lines: single and double knockouts.
* Design and execute targeted knock-in strategies, including donor design, delivery optimization, and editing-efficiency assessment.
* Genotype and validate edits by sequencing, qPCR or digital PCR, and protein-level readouts.

**Stable cell line generation**

* Perform transient transfections to test constructs quickly, optimizing reagent, nucleic acid amount, and harvest timing, and confirming expression before committing to a stable line.
* Generate stable lines using viral and non-viral delivery; perform clonal selection, expansion, functional validation, and banking.
* Characterize clones for expression level, assay performance, and stability over passage.

**Cell-based assay development**

* Develop, optimize, and run functional assays: plate-based, reporter and proximity-based assays; flow cytometry; and other cellular functional readouts.
* Optimize seeding density, stimulation conditions, dose range, incubation time, controls, and acceptance criteria to improve sensitivity, dynamic range, and reproducibility.
* Prepare test articles, reagents, controls, and assay plates according to established protocols and study plans .

**Data, documentation, and communication**

* Analyze dose-response data, fit curves, assess assay quality (Z', signal window, variability), and flag trends, outliers, and deviations.
* Keep complete, timely records in the electronic lab notebook, consistent with data-integrity expectations.
* Present results at team meetings and contribute figures and data to technical reports.

**Lab operations**

* Troubleshoot routine assay and culture

**Reports to:** Director of Quality Management

**Department:** Quality & Food Safety

**Location:** Marysville, California

**FLSA Classification:** Hourly, Non-Exempt

**Compensation:** $27.00 - $31.50/hour

### **About the Company**

Paleovalley and Wild Pastures were born from a simple but radical idea: real food can heal — people, animals, and the planet. When Paleovalley co-founders Autumn and Chas Smith saw how industrialized food was affecting human health and the health of the land, they refused to play along. Autumn’s own journey of healing through nutrient-dense foods lit a fire that became Paleovalley. From there, the mission grew roots, sprouted wings, and eventually expanded into Wild Pastures to bring regeneratively raised meats directly to families nationwide.

Today, Paleovalley crafts deeply nourishing snacks and supplements made with organic ingredients and honorable sourcing. Wild Pastures connects small American farmers practicing regenerative agriculture with customers who believe better food is worth fighting for. Every product, every partnership, and every decision is guided by a commitment to real ingredients, regenerative practices, and the belief that health is built from the soil up.

We’re a team of grounded doers, curious thinkers, bold builders, and warm humans who like to laugh while doing meaningful work. We're growing quickly, fueled by purpose and a shared desire to repair the food system one thoughtful choice at a time. If you feel energized by impact, drawn to mission, and ready to join a company rewriting the future of food, we’d love to meet you!

### **About the Opportunity**

The Quality Control Technician serves as the primary onsite Quality & Food Safety representative at their assigned Paleovalley and Wild Pastures warehouse. This hands-on technical role helps ensure products are received, stored, handled, and shipped in accordance with company quality standards, product specifications, food safety requirements, and applicable FDA and USDA requirements.

Working independently onsite and in close partnership with the broader Quality & Food Safety team, the Quality Control Technician performs and evaluates Quality inspections and verification activities, addresses routine Quality issues within established procedures and authority, initiates Quality holds when needed, maintains accurate Quality records, and escalates elevated-risk or complex FSQA concerns to their supervisor. The role also identifies trends, recurring issues, and opportunities to strengthen onsite Quality processes and controls.

### **What You’ll Do**

* Serve as the primary onsite Quality & Food Safety resource for the assigned warehouse, independently applying established standards and technical knowledge to identify, address, document, and escalate Quality and compliance concerns.
* Perform routine Quality and Food Safety inspections of incoming, stored, returned, and outbound Paleovalley and Wild Pastures products and shipments, including transportation conditions, packaging, labels and lot information, shelf life, temperatures, and other established criteria.
* Collect product samples as needed in accordance with established procedures and coordinate shipment to approved laboratories for testing.
* Control nonconforming or potentially compromised product by initiating Quality & Food Safety holds or quarantine, maintaining required documentation and product controls, and coordinating with the supervisor on disposition and release decisions.
* Conduct warehouse Quality & Food Safety verification activities, monitoring GMPs, sanitation, pest control, storage and segregation, temperature controls, product rotation, allergen/cross-contact controls, and other conditions that may affect product safety, quality, or compliance; maintain applicable pest-control accounts and records.
* Maintain accurate Quality and Food Safety records and data in Acumatica and other approved systems, including inspections, holds, nonconformances, temperatures, product conditions, and supporting documentation; identify trends or recurring concerns requiring follow-up.
* Document product-quality concerns and support supervisor-led investigations, including customer returns, damaged or compromised product, freight damage, and other nonconformances by gathering relevant records, observations, photographs, and supporting information.
* Support traceability, mock recalls, recalls, corrective actions, and audit preparation by locating and verifying affected product and records and gathering required documentation under the direction of the supervisor.
* Observe adherence to established Quality & Food Safety requirements throughout warehouse operations and promptly escalate identified gaps or concerns for appropriate follow-up, guidance, or training.
* Identify trends and recommend improvements to onsite Quality and Food Safety processes, controls, procedures, and documentation; support implementation of approved changes with the Quality & Food Safety team.
* Independently manage routine onsite Quality activities and issues using technical judgment within defined authority, escalating elevated-risk, complex, novel, or regulatory-sensitive FSQA matters to the supervisor.

### **What You’ll Need to Succeed**

* High school diploma or GED required; associate degree, technical training, or coursework in Food Science, Food Safety, Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, or a related field preferred.
* 3+ years of progressively responsible experience in food quality control, quality assurance, food safety, food manufacturing, distribution Quality, or a related regulated environment; equivalent combinations of relevant education, training, and experience will be considered.
* Strong working knowledge of food safety, quality, sanitation, GMPs, and applicable Quality requirements within a regulated food manufacturing, warehousing, or distribution environment.
* Demonstrated ability to independently apply specifications, SOPs
